subproblem.title: Gradient bound for mollified functions on inner parallel sets (Simon 2.5)
subproblem.statement: For every n ∈ ℕ, every open W ⊆ ℝⁿ, every set K ⊆ ℝⁿ, every u integrable on W, every σ ∈ ℝ and every kernel ρ : ℝⁿ → ℝ of class C² with ρ ≥ 0, support ρ ⊆ B(0,σ) (open ball) and ∫ρ = 1, if closedBall(x,σ) ⊆ W for every x ∈ K then, with w := ρ * (1_W u) (Mathlib convolution ρ (W.indicator u) (lsmul ℝ ℝ) volume, i.e. w(x) = ∫ ρ(t)(1_W u)(x − t) dt), ∫⁻_K ‖Dw(x)‖ dx ≤ |Du|(W) := SimonGMT bvVariationOn u W in [0,∞]; here Dw = fderiv ℝ w and ‖·‖ is the operator norm.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n : ℕ) (W K : Set (Rn n)) (u ρ : Rn n → ℝ) (σ : ℝ), IsOpen W → IntegrableOn u W volume → ContDiff ℝ 2 ρ → (∀ x, 0 ≤ ρ x) → Function.support ρ ⊆ ball 0 σ → ∫ x, ρ x = 1 → (∀ x ∈ K, closedBall x σ ⊆ W) → ∫⁻ x in K, ‖fderiv ℝ (convolution ρ (W.indicator u) (ContinuousLinearMap.lsmul ℝ ℝ) volume) x‖ₑ ≤ Chapter02.bvVariationOn u W
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof, Section T, steps T4 (variation of a mollification), T5 (smooth duality) and T6 (gradient bound: ∫_{W^(σ)} |∇(φ_σ*(u1_W))| ≤ |Du|(W)). These carry out the computation in Simon's printed proof of Lemma 2.5:
“for fixed smooth g with |g| ≤ f and σ < dist(spt f, ∂U): ∫ g·∇u_(σ) = −∫ u_(σ) div g = −∫ φ_σ * u div g = −∫ u φ_σ * div g = −∫ u div(φ_σ * g)”, together with “(4) ∫ f|Du_(σ)| = sup_{|g|≤f, g smooth} ∫ g·∇u_(σ)”.
Two adaptations: the fixed mollifier φ_σ is replaced by an arbitrary C² kernel ρ ≥ 0 with ∫ρ = 1 and support in B(0,σ) (no symmetry is assumed; the reflected kernel ρ̌ is used instead), and the inner parallel set W^(σ) is replaced by the hypothesis “closedBall(x,σ) ⊆ W for x ∈ K”.

Notation. E := ℝⁿ = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n), μ := volume (Lebesgue measure, invariant under translations and under x ↦ −x). Dh(x) := fderiv ℝ h x. div h := Chapter02.euclideanDivergence h = trace Dh. |Du|(W) := Chapter02.bvVariationOn u W is the supremum, over g ∈ C_c(E,E) that are Lipschitz (IsLipschitzTestField) with tsupport g ⊆ W and compactlySupportedSupNorm g ≤ 1, of ofReal(∫_W u div g).

0. Preliminaries.
 - F := 1_W u = W.indicator u. W is open, hence measurable, so F ∈ L¹(E) (integrable_indicator_iff).
 - Since ∫ρ = 1, we have ρ ≢ 0, so B(0,σ) ≠ ∅ and σ > 0. tsupport ρ ⊆ closedBall(0,σ) is compact, ρ is bounded, and ρ is Lipschitz (C¹ with compact support).
 - ρ̌(x) := ρ(−x) has the same properties: C², ρ̌ ≥ 0, support ρ̌ ⊆ B(0,σ) (the ball is symmetric), and ∫ρ̌ = ∫ρ = 1 (μ is invariant under negation).
 - w := ρ * F = convolution ρ F (lsmul ℝ ℝ) volume, so w(x) = ∫ ρ(t)F(x − t) dt. w is C² (Mathlib HasCompactSupport.contDiff_convolution_left with ρ C² of compact support and F locally integrable); in particular w is C¹.
 - O := {x ∈ E : closedBall(x,σ) ⊆ W}. O is open: if closedBall(x,σ) ⊆ W, then since closedBall(x,σ) is compact and W open there is r > 0 with cthickening(r, closedBall(x,σ)) ⊆ W (Mathlib IsCompact.exists_cthickening_subset_open), and then closedBall(x',σ) ⊆ W whenever ‖x' − x‖ ≤ r. By hypothesis K ⊆ O.
 - Put M := |Du|(W). If M = ∞ there is nothing to prove. Assume M < ∞ and let m := M.toReal ≥ 0, so that ofReal m = M.

1. Duality bound for one test field (T4). Claim: for every C¹ field g : E → E with compact support, tsupport g ⊆ O and ‖g(x)‖ ≤ 1 for all x, we have ∫ w(x) div g(x) dx ≤ m.
 (a) Fubini. Let h := div g. Since g is C¹ with compact support, Dg is continuous with compact support, so h is bounded, measurable, and h = 0 off tsupport g. The function (x,t) ↦ ρ(t)F(x − t)h(x) is integrable on E × E: by Tonelli and translation invariance, ∫∫ ρ(t)|F(x − t)||h(x)| dx dt ≤ sup|h|·∫ρ·‖F‖₁ < ∞. Hence, using Fubini and the substitution x = s + t for fixed t,
   ∫ w h = ∫_t ρ(t) ∫_s F(s) h(s + t) ds dt = ∫_s F(s) (∫_t ρ(t) h(s + t) dt) ds = ∫_s F(s)·(ρ̌ * h)(s) ds,
 because ∫_t ρ(t) h(s + t) dt = ∫_t ρ(−t) h(s − t) dt = (ρ̌ * h)(s) (substitute t ↦ −t).
 (b) Divergence commutes with convolution. Let G := ρ̌ * g, the vector-valued convolution convolution ρ̌ g (lsmul ℝ ℝ) volume, so G(s) = ∫ ρ̌(t) g(s − t) dt. Since g is C¹ with compact support and ρ̌ is locally integrable, Mathlib HasCompactSupport.hasFDerivAt_convolution_right gives DG(s) = ∫ ρ̌(t) Dg(s − t) dt for every s, and G is C¹ (HasCompactSupport.contDiff_convolution_right). The trace is a continuous linear map on the finite-dimensional space E →L[ℝ] E, so it commutes with the Bochner integral (ContinuousLinearMap.integral_comp_comm). Hence div G(s) = ∫ ρ̌(t) div g(s − t) dt = (ρ̌ * h)(s) for every s.
 (c) G is admissible for W.
 - Support: support G ⊆ support ρ̌ + support g ⊆ closedBall(0,σ) + tsupport g (Mathlib support_convolution_subset). The right side is compact (a sum of compact sets), hence closed, so tsupport G ⊆ closedBall(0,σ) + tsupport g. Every y ∈ tsupport g lies in O, so y + closedBall(0,σ) = closedBall(y,σ) ⊆ W. Hence tsupport G ⊆ W, and G has compact support.
 - G is continuous with compact support, so it defines an element of C_c(E,E). It is C¹ with compact support, hence Lipschitz (ContDiff.lipschitzWith_of_hasCompactSupport), i.e. IsLipschitzTestField.
 - ‖G(s)‖ ≤ ∫ ρ̌(t)‖g(s − t)‖ dt ≤ ∫ρ̌ = 1 for every s (since ρ̌ ≥ 0). So compactlySupportedSupNorm G = sSup (range ‖G(·)‖) ≤ 1 (csSup_le; the range is nonempty).
 (d) By SimonGMT ofReal_integral_le_bvVariationOn, ofReal(∫_W u div G) ≤ M = ofReal m. Since m ≥ 0, this gives ∫_W u div G ≤ m (ENNReal.ofReal_le_ofReal_iff).
 Finally, by (a) and (b), ∫ w h = ∫ F·div G = ∫ 1_W u·div G = ∫_W u div G ≤ m.

2. Smooth duality on compact subsets of O (T5). Claim: for every compact L ⊆ O, ∫_L ‖Dw(x)‖ dx ≤ m.
 (a) A smooth cut-off. Choose r > 0 with cthickening(3r, L) ⊆ O (IsCompact.exists_cthickening_subset_open). Let ϑ be a C^∞ kernel with ϑ ≥ 0, support ϑ ⊆ B(0,r) and ∫ϑ = 1; for instance ϑ := c.normed volume for the ContDiffBump c centred at 0 with rIn = r/2 and rOut = r (Mathlib contDiff_normed, nonneg_normed, support_normed_eq, integral_normed). Put χ := ϑ * 1_{thickening(r,L)}. Then:
 - χ is C^∞ (HasCompactSupport.contDiff_convolution_left), and 0 ≤ χ ≤ 1;
 - χ = 1 on L, because for x ∈ L and ‖t‖ < r we have x − t ∈ thickening(r,L);
 - support χ ⊆ B(0,r) + thickening(r,L) ⊆ thickening(2r,L), so tsupport χ ⊆ cthickening(2r,L) ⊆ O, which is compact.
 (b) The test field. Let ∇w(x) ∈ E be the gradient, i.e. the Riesz representative of Dw(x), so that Dw(x)[v] = ⟨∇w(x), v⟩ and ‖∇w(x)‖ = ‖Dw(x)‖. Since w is C² and the Riesz map is a linear isometry, ∇w is C¹. Fix η > 0 and put
   g(x) := −χ(x)·∇w(x)/√(‖∇w(x)‖² + η²).
 g is C¹: the denominator is C¹ and ≥ η > 0, and χ is C^∞. Also tsupport g ⊆ tsupport χ ⊆ O is compact, and ‖g(x)‖ ≤ ‖∇w(x)‖/√(‖∇w(x)‖² + η²) ≤ 1. So by step 1, ∫ w div g ≤ m.
 (c) Evaluation by integration by parts. g is C¹ with compact support, hence Lipschitz, and w is C¹. By the sibling theorem Submission.bv_lipschitz_integration_by_parts (with F := w),
   ∫ w div g = −∫ Dw(x)[g(x)] dx = ∫ χ(x)·‖∇w(x)‖²/√(‖∇w(x)‖² + η²) dx,
 because Dw(x)[∇w(x)] = ‖∇w(x)‖².
 (d) Lower bound. For t ≥ 0 we have t²/√(t² + η²) ≥ t − η: if t ≤ η the left side is ≥ 0 ≥ t − η; if t > η then t²/√(t² + η²) ≥ t²/(t + η) ≥ (t² − η²)/(t + η) = t − η. Since χ ≥ 0 everywhere and χ = 1 on L, pointwise χ·‖∇w‖²/√(‖∇w‖² + η²) ≥ 1_L·(‖∇w‖ − η). All functions involved are continuous with compact support, hence integrable. Thus
   ∫_L ‖Dw‖ − η·μ(L) ≤ ∫ w div g ≤ m.
 Since η > 0 is arbitrary and μ(L) < ∞, we get ∫_L ‖Dw‖ ≤ m.

3. Passage to O and to K.
 Choose compact sets L_1 ⊆ L_2 ⊆ … (l = 1, 2, …) with ∪_l L_l = O: take L_l := {x ∈ closedBall(0,l) : infDist(x, Oᶜ) ≥ 1/l} if O ≠ E, and L_l := closedBall(0,l) if O = E. Each L_l is closed (infDist is continuous) and bounded, hence compact. It is contained in O, because infDist(x, Oᶜ) > 0 forces x ∉ Oᶜ (Oᶜ is closed). Their union is O, because every x ∈ O has infDist(x, Oᶜ) > 0 (O is open).
 For each l, ∫⁻_{L_l} ‖Dw‖ₑ = ofReal(∫_{L_l} ‖Dw‖) ≤ ofReal m = M by step 2; the integrand is continuous on a compact set, hence integrable. The measurable functions 1_{L_l}·‖Dw‖ₑ increase pointwise to 1_O·‖Dw‖ₑ. So by monotone convergence (Mathlib lintegral_iSup), ∫⁻_O ‖Dw‖ₑ = sup_l ∫⁻_{L_l} ‖Dw‖ₑ ≤ M.
 Finally K ⊆ O, so ∫⁻_K ‖Dw‖ₑ ≤ ∫⁻_O ‖Dw‖ₑ ≤ M (lintegral_mono_set; no measurability of K is needed). Here ‖Dw‖ₑ is the extended norm of fderiv ℝ w x, as in the statement. ∎

Edge cases. If W = ∅ then O = ∅ and K = ∅ (each x ∈ K satisfies x ∈ closedBall(x,σ) ⊆ W), so the left side is 0. If n = 0 then Dw = 0. Both cases are also covered by the general argument.
proof_key_steps: Set F = 1_W u ∈ L¹, w = ρ * F ∈ C², ρ̌(x) = ρ(−x), and the open set O = {x : closedBall(x,σ) ⊆ W} ⊇ K; assume |Du|(W) = ofReal m < ∞.
T4: for C¹ g with compact support in O and |g| ≤ 1, Fubini gives ∫ w div g = ∫ F (ρ̌ * div g) = ∫_W u div(ρ̌ * g), and ρ̌ * g is an admissible Lipschitz field for W; hence ∫ w div g ≤ m.

T5: for compact L ⊆ O, take g = −χ∇w/√(|∇w|²+η²) with a smooth cut-off χ (χ = 1 on L, tsupport χ ⊆ O); integrate by parts with Submission.bv_lipschitz_integration_by_parts to get ∫_L |∇w| − ηLⁿ(L) ≤ m.
Let η → 0, exhaust O by compacts (monotone convergence) and restrict to K ⊆ O: ∫⁻_K ‖Dw‖ₑ ≤ |Du|(W).

audit.reason: The reflected-kernel argument correctly removes symmetry. C² regularity suffices for the C¹ dual test field. Support control, integration by parts and compact exhaustion establish the bound; restriction monotonicity handles arbitrary, possibly nonmeasurable K. Only the declared integration-by-parts dependency is needed.
